intent: "Show me this campaign" — settings, senders, schedule and timezone policy, pacing, reply policy, declared successor, and the count of people in each state.

input_schema.title: campaign.get input
input_schema.description: A campaign is named either by the identifier Jason already holds for it or, the first time, by one the planner supplies.

external_id.description: The provider's own identifier, given to link a campaign for the first time. Later calls work by the pin.

external_ids.description: Only this plugin's own pins reach it, so another provider's identifier is never visible here.

status.description: `other` is the honest answer for a provider state this vocabulary has no word for; the provider's own word belongs under `vendor`.

counts.description: An empty object is a real answer: it says the provider reports no counts, which is not the same as reporting zero.

vendor.description: The provider's own answer, untranslated and untyped, so nothing is lost while the neutral part stays strict.

campaign.description: The provider's identifier for the campaign this read resolved, pinned so every later operation works by it.

failure_codes.when: The provider holds no campaign under the identifier this call carried.
The plugin's own credential does not let it read campaigns for this account.
The provider refused the read for now and it may be asked again.
The provider could not be reached, or answered with a failure on its own side.
The provider was called and no answer arrived. A read changes nothing and costs nothing, so the next attempt simply asks again.

conformance: A call carrying only `campaign.external_ids.campaign` answers, so a linked campaign never needs the planner to repeat the provider's identifier.
A call carrying only `args.campaign.external_id` answers and returns that identifier under `external_ids.campaign`, which is how the first link is made.
A campaign the provider does not hold fails `campaign_not_found` as permanent, rather than succeeding with an empty result.
A provider state this vocabulary has no word for is reported as `other`, with the provider's own word under `vendor`.
The result carries no field this contract does not declare, apart from whatever sits under `vendor`.
